mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates a strengthening demand in the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances where HOUST showed a sustained increase over the previous 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a quarter signals an improving labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.5% in the previous quarter.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates a robust supply-side response, which boosts economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals a consumer-driven demand surge, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS growth exceeded GDPC1 growth in the previous quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period signals a disinflationary environment, which reduces input costs and increases corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances where CPIAUCSL showed a sustained decrease over the previous 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year growth rate of GDP (GDPC1) exceeds the year-over-year growth rate of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2%, it signals real economic growth outpacing inflation, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > CPIAUCSL YoY growth by > 2%
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 YoY growth exceeded CPIAUCSL YoY growth by more than 2%.
